about: The golden recall corpus (test/memory-recall-golden.test.js): the memory a person built over months on a web shop, a second project of theirs and the claims that hold in every project. Each entry is one claim, filed in order: `by` who said it (owner: the user's own word, the default; model: an assistant's note; learner: learned from a session, inferred), `replaces` the key of the claim it corrects (filed by correcting that one), `forget` retired after filing. A key is how the cases name a claim; the test maps it to the id memory gave it.

claims.text: Never add a Co-Authored-By trailer to commit messages.
The user works in VS Code on Windows 11 with PowerShell as the default shell.
The user prefers short answers that lead with the result.
Never force-push to the main branch; open a pull request instead.
Never edit a database migration that has been merged; add a new migration instead.
Never commit .env files or API keys to the repository.
Always run pnpm lint before committing.
The user prefers small pull requests that change one concern each.
The user wants a failing test written before every bug fix.
Branch names follow feature/<ticket>-<slug>, for example feature/SHOP-412-cart-badge.
Commit messages follow Conventional Commits: feat:, fix:, chore:.
Styles are written with Tailwind utility classes; no new CSS files are added.
API errors are returned as { error: { code, message } } with a matching HTTP status.
Money is stored as integer cents in the database, never as floats.
The API server listens on port 3000 in development.
The API server listens on port 8080 in development.
The storefront's Vite dev server runs on port 5173.
Storybook runs on port 6006 with pnpm storybook.
The main database is PostgreSQL 16; the local connection string is DATABASE_URL in .env.
The staging database runs on db-staging.internal and is refreshed from production every Sunday night.
Database access goes through Prisma; the schema is prisma/schema.prisma.
Redis holds the session store and the rate-limit counters.
Background jobs run on BullMQ workers, started with pnpm worker.
Order confirmation emails are sent through SendGrid.
Order confirmation emails are sent through Postmark; templates live in emails/templates.
Invoices are rendered to PDF by Puppeteer in src/billing/invoice-pdf.ts.
Payments go through Stripe; the webhook handler is src/payments/stripe-webhook.ts.
In Stripe test mode the card 4242 4242 4242 4242 makes a successful charge.
Sales tax is calculated by TaxJar at checkout, for US addresses only.
Product search is served by Meilisearch, reindexed every night by jobs/reindex.ts.
Product images are stored in the S3 bucket shop-media-prod and served through CloudFront.
Customer login uses Auth0; the callback route is /auth/callback.
The admin panel at /admin uses separate staff accounts with two-factor authentication required.
The admin panel lives at /backoffice and staff share one login.
CI runs on GitHub Actions; the main workflow is .github/workflows/ci.yml.
Production deploys go out from the release branch through Heroku.
Production deploys go out from the main branch through Render, once CI passes.
Every pull request gets a preview environment on Render.
The project runs on Node 22; the version is pinned in .nvmrc.
The project uses npm as its package manager.
The project uses pnpm as its package manager.
Unit tests run with Vitest: pnpm test.
End-to-end tests use Playwright and live in e2e/; run them with pnpm e2e.
Feature flags come from LaunchDarkly through src/lib/flags.ts.
Product analytics events are sent to PostHog from src/lib/analytics.ts.
Runtime errors are reported to Sentry; the DSN is SENTRY_DSN.
Production server logs are shipped to Better Stack.
The storefront is translated into English, German and French with i18next; strings live in locales/.
Prices are shown in USD, EUR and GBP; exchange rates are fetched hourly from Open Exchange Rates.
Shipping rates come from Shippo; orders over $75 ship free.
Inventory is synced from the warehouse ERP every 15 minutes by jobs/inventory-sync.ts.
A guest's cart is kept in Redis for 30 days; a signed-in customer's cart is saved in Postgres.
Discount codes are stored in the coupons table; a code can be limited to first orders.
Product reviews are moderated before they are published; the moderation queue is at /admin/reviews.
The mobile app is built with React Native and Expo in apps/mobile.
The repository is a pnpm workspace: apps/web, apps/api, apps/mobile and packages/ui.
Shared React components live in packages/ui and are documented in Storybook.
CloudFront caches product pages for 5 minutes; updating a product purges its page.
Scheduled jobs are defined in apps/api/src/cron.ts and run in UTC.
Production database backups are taken nightly and kept for 30 days.
Customer support tickets are handled in Zendesk; its widget loads on the help page.
Customer data deletion requests are processed by jobs/gdpr-erase.ts within 30 days.
The storefront's performance budget is a Lighthouse score of 90 on mobile.
The sitemap is generated at build time into public/sitemap.xml.
The public API is rate limited to 100 requests per minute per IP address.
Partners receive order webhooks signed with HMAC-SHA256, with a secret per partner.
Priya owns the checkout product decisions; design questions go to Marco.
The on-call rotation lives in PagerDuty; incident write-ups go in docs/incidents/.
Local Postgres, Redis and Meilisearch start with docker compose up -d.
Local sample data is loaded with pnpm db:seed.
TypeScript strict mode is on in every package.
The REST API is described in OpenAPI at apps/api/openapi.yaml.
Order timestamps are stored in UTC and shown in the shop's timezone, Europe/Berlin.
We chose Redis over Memcached for sessions because Redis survives restarts.
We moved from TypeORM to Prisma for its type-safe client.
We host on Render rather than AWS ECS to keep operations small.
We picked Meilisearch over Elasticsearch because it is lighter to run.
The storefront stays a single-page app; server-side rendering was turned down for now.
How to cut a release: 1. pnpm changeset version 2. git push --follow-tags 3. wait for Render to deploy main
How to ship a hotfix: 1. branch from main as hotfix/<slug> 2. open a pull request labelled urgent 3. merge after one review
How to add a database migration: 1. edit prisma/schema.prisma 2. pnpm prisma migrate dev --name <slug> 3. commit the new migration folder
How to rotate the Stripe API key: 1. create a restricted key in the Stripe dashboard 2. set STRIPE_SECRET_KEY on Render 3. revoke the old key
Moving checkout to the Stripe Payment Element is half done: the address step still uses the old form.
Meilisearch typo tolerance still needs tuning for short SKU queries.
The Postmark move still needs the password-reset email template.
Guest carts live in Redis for 30 days, and signed-in customers' carts are stored in Postgres.
Use Node.js 22 here, as pinned by .nvmrc.
Store prices in whole cents as integers, not as floating point numbers.
Vitest runs the unit tests (pnpm test).
